# skade

> A fast, pure-Rust Iceberg lakehouse — a multicore data plane (Arrow `RecordBatch`
> in, DataFusion SQL out) over **skade-katalog**, an embedded single-file ACID Iceberg
> catalog (redb): no JVM, no REST catalog service, no network hop.

⚡ **GATLING** — one all-core engine · zero rayon · zero-copy · ~11/12 cores

## Mashup — an all-core data plane over an embedded catalog

skade's data plane fans Parquet encoding across **every core** — the gatling
no-barrier fork-join engine (`znippy-zoomies gatling_forkjoin`): all cores encode,
one sequential writer commits — so ingest **saturates the box** instead of pinning
a single writer thread. Same 1M-row dataset, same box, three writers:

**skade vs stock Iceberg vs raw Parquet — `oxr`, 1M rows, `loki` · 12 cores:**

| writer | write (M rows/s) | read (M rows/s) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **skade** — gatling all-core encode + snapshot commit | **35.4** | 58.3 |
| Iceberg — stock `iceberg-rust` writer, same catalog | 9.8 | 42.1 |
| raw Parquet — `ArrowWriter`, no catalog / no snapshots | 12.6 | 86.0 |

skade writes **3.6× stock Iceberg** and **2.8× raw Parquet** on the same hardware,
because the gatling encode holds **~12/12 cores** (`skade.ingest_parallel_scaling`:
12/12 cores busy, 95% peak CPU) where a single-writer path pins one.

And the embedded catalog itself — a single redb file, no Nessie/Polaris service to
stand up — reads *faster* than either service:

**`table_exists` — 2.0M ops/s, ~492× Nessie · ~677× Polaris, 0.31 µs p50.**
